title: Distinguish regen-safe generated-only dirt from user-prose edits
context: Grounding docs that went stale-dirty once stayed stale forever, requiring manual chore commits on every release. The prior clean-only refresh rule couldn't distinguish between 'stale generated section' and 'user edit', so it skipped all dirty docs to avoid clobbering user work. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: For marker-managed docs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, …), compare worktree vs HEAD with the managed HUNCH section stripped from both. Equal outside the block ⇒ safe to regenerate. For wholly-owned rule files, any tracked content is generated. Protects user prose while healing stranded docs.
consequences: Stale-dirty docs auto-heal on next capture flush, ending the manual-chore treadmill
Release gate clean-tree checks no longer need workarounds
User prose is always protected by prose-outside-block equality check
Wholly-owned files get simpler, faster treatment (no comparison needed)
Byte-equivalent regenerations still stage (commit re-syncs HEAD↔worktree)
alternatives_rejected: Regenerate all dirty docs (risks clobbering user edits)
Skip all dirty docs forever (leaves drift and blocks releases)
Manual user intervention on every stale doc (ergonomically worse)
